logical_form: Sample S is taken from population P. Sample S is a very small part of population P. Conclusion C is drawn from sample S and applied to population P.

X is true because of Y.

Y is true because of X.
A lot of people believe X.Therefore, X must be true.

Person 1 is claiming Y.

Person 1 is a moron.

Therefore, Y is not true.
If A is true, then B is true. B is true. Therefore, A is true.
Claim X is made without evidence. In place of evidence, emotion is used to convince the interlocutor that X is true.
Either X or Y is true.

Term X is used to mean Y in the premise.
Term X is used to mean Z in the conclusion.
Person 1 makes claim Y. Person 2 restates person 1’s claim (in a distorted way). Person 2 attacks the distorted version of the claim. Therefore, claim Y is false.

According to person 1, who is an expert on the issue of Y, Y is true.
Therefore, Y is true.
Person 1 knows claim X is incorrect. They still claim that X is correct using an incorrect argument
Argument A is presented by person 1. Person 2 introduces argument B. Argument A is abandoned.
X occurred after Y. Therefore, Y caused X (although X was also a result of A,B,C,… etc)
